label: early-to-mid copy phase (recall 2-5), favoring inputs t/f/m/x/p/o/j/r/z/k
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L), never on original tokens, the delimiter, or the first copy step (recall_idx 0). 92% of activation mass falls at recall_idx 2-5, peaking at 3-4. Inside that window only about 17% of steps fire, and the input token picks which ones: t and f have the highest rates (~15%, 3x lift over all steps), then m, x, p, o, j, r, z, k. Never fires when the input is the first occurrence of that token in the sequence (in_first=0 always), which is consistent with copy-phase inputs. Strongest examples are L=3 sequences at recall 2 with input f/p/t (e.g. c f t <DEL> c [f]). Short sequences (L=3) have the highest rate (32%). Rate also varies with absolute t (peaks at t=6 and t=10-13), which the predicate does not capture. The window alone gives recall 0.93 at precision 0.17; adding the token set gives F1 ~0.45, mass recall ~0.68 on dev. The remaining token/position interaction was not resolved.
